chunks: From him, from Ibn Muskaan, from a man from the people of Al-Jabal whom he did not name, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Adhere to the original (of religion), and beware of every newly invented matter for which there is no pledge, nor trust, nor guarantee, nor covenant. And be cautious of the people whom you rely upon for yourself, for the people are the enemies of the bounties.'

key_terms.التِّلَاد: The original, authentic, or established (referring to the core of religion)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'people are the enemies of bounties'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) advises adhering to the 'tilad' (original, unadulterated practices) while avoiding innovators who lack religious covenant and trustworthiness. He warns that people are often 'enemies of bounties,' meaning they may reject or distort divine favors, thus urging caution even towards those one personally trusts.
